    The mesh complex K and its collapse #

    Subsection 4.1 (subsec:mesh-walk-cover, scalar-normalization.tex): "For every nonprojective vertex X, adjoin an edge t_X : τX → X to the underlying graph of Γ. For each arrow a : Y → X with X nonprojective, attach a triangle with boundary (σa) a t_X⁻¹." Its fundamental groupoid is Morse.Pi (meshTris Q).

    The proof of Lemma 4.2 (lem:mesh-walk-free, lines 96–113) eliminates edges and triangles. Here the eliminations are an acyclic matching (meshMatching):

    • an arrow whose mate orbit is a finite chain is eliminated with its own triangle, from the end of the chain ("Along a chain, the triangles successively express all but one quiver edge in terms of that edge and the edges t_X. Eliminate these edges and triangles from one end of the chain"); the potential is the remaining length of the chain;
    • on the arrows with cyclic mate orbits (the periodic components) the matching is read off from a depth function e on vertices that is invariant under τ and such that each vertex has at most one cyclic incoming arrow from a vertex of depth at most its own: the triangle of the arrow from the parent eliminates t_X, the other triangles eliminate their arrow. This is the combinatorial form of "a periodic component containing arrows gives a mapping torus, which retracts onto its core circle"; the depth function is constructed from the tree model in PeriodicDepth.lean.

    Once every triangle is eliminated, the remaining complex is a graph and the vertex groups are free (Morse.isFreeGroup_end).
